newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israelis rally for Hebron, talks with PLO drag on.
newsitem.headline: Israelis rally for Hebron, talks with PLO drag on.

text.p: Thousands of right-wing Israelis rallied against a withdrawal from the West Bank town of Hebron on Tuesday as talks with the PLO on implementing the redeployment dragged on.
Israeli and Palestinian leaders said they were determined to reach a deal despite the absence from the region of Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and a key U.S. mediator.
"Arafat delegated us. We have his instructions and we are in touch with him every hour on the hour," said negotiator Saeb Erekat after talks with Israeli counterparts in Tel Aviv.
"President Arafat's instruction is for us to reach the agreement as soon as possible on the implementation protocol."
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu accused the PLO of delaying an agreement, saying the Palestinians were confident Israel would be blamed for any foot-dragging.

"One of the reasons the Palestinian side is holding up its completion is that it assumes...any time the Arab side alleges there is a problem in moving forward, Israel's government will be blamed," Netanyahu said in a speech in Tel Aviv.
U.S. envoy Dennis Ross, ending three weeks of marathon mediation in a bid to nail down details of the long-delayed pullout from the West Bank town, left for Washington on Tuesday.
Arafat was on a European tour to seek backing for the 1993 peace pact with Israel on Palestinian self-rule. He was expected back in Palestinian-ruled Gaza at the end of the week.

In Jerusalem, right-wing Jews, many wearing the skullcaps of religious Jews, called on the government to cancel the deal with the PLO and marched to the American consulate to protest what they said was U.S. pressure on Israel.

"We hope the government will stay strong and have the courage not to turn over parts of the city of our fathers to the hands of terrorists," said Dov Lior, rabbi of the Kiryat Arba settlement near Hebron, a town holy to Jews and Moslems.
Authorities sealed off Jerusalem's busiest downtown street for the rally and police said 1,200 law enforcers were on hand to preserve order.

"Mr Clinton, Israel is not a banana republic," read one sign held up by a demonstrator. "(Warren) Christopher, we won't let you turn Israel into a reservation for endangered Jews" read another, referring to the U.S. secretary of state.
Israel has said modifications of a pullout deal signed by the previous Labour-led government were needed to safeguard the 400 Jews who live and study in Hebron under heavy guard among 100,000 Arabs.
Differences centred on Israel's demand for the right to pursue militants into parts of Hebron it hands over, and what arms PLO police would be allowed to carry, Palestinians said.
In Hebron on Tuesday, Jewish settlers shouting "Hebron is ours" shoved, cursed and spat at PLO officials who toured the flashpoint town, Arab and Israeli witnesses said.
Israeli paratroops shepherded the officials to their car, which drove them to safety.
Violence also erupted in a West Bank village after the funeral of a 10-year-old Palestinian boy who relatives said had been killed by a Jewish settler on Sunday.

About 50 masked mourners threw rocks at Israeli cars travelling on a road below used by Jewish settlers. Other mourners joined in and soldiers responded by firing live ammunition, rubber bullets and teargas, witnesses said.

"Get the Nazis out of our land," read one banner at the burial attended by 5,000 mourners who vowed to avenge the killing of Hilmi Shosha. Arab witnesses said a settler had beaten the boy unconscious on suspicion of throwing stones.
A Jerusalem court ordered the settler, Nahum Kurman, held in police custody until Friday, pending an indictment.
